title: Net-banking login requested to "credit" a joining bonus vs. payroll collecting account number and IFSC only
summary: A caller from Vistara Infotech's payroll team phones a new joiner about their joining bonus. In the fraud case, the caller says the bonus can be credited today only if the joiner shares their net-banking user ID and password so payroll can "link" the account. In the legitimate case, payroll asks for the account number, IFSC, and name as per bank records, to be entered on the HR portal with a cancelled-cheque image, and states that the bonus is paid with the first salary and no password, PIN, or OTP is ever needed.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a recent joiner; details sampled at generation.
other_facts: Role: software engineer who joined in the last one to two weeks, CTC [AMOUNT_1] (₹6,00,000–₹12,00,000 per year).
Joining bonus: [AMOUNT_2] (₹10,000–₹50,000), stated in the offer letter.
Both calls mention the bonus amount, "bank account", "IFSC", "credit", and "today".

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks for net-banking login credentials. Nobody needs a password to send money to an account; genuine entities never ask for it.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the login and take money from the account.
stable_facts: Caller knows the joiner's name, joining date, and bonus amount.
Caller says the payroll system needs to "link and verify" the salary account "through net banking".
Caller says the bonus batch closes today; otherwise it moves to next quarter.

legitimate.label_rationale: Payroll asks only for the details needed to send money (account number, IFSC, name), through the company portal, and states that credentials are never needed.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get bank details entered so salary and bonus can be paid.
stable_facts: Details are entered on https://hr.vistara-infotech.invalid with a cancelled-cheque or passbook image.
Bonus is paid with the first salary if details are in by the payroll cut-off (this week).
Payroll never asks for passwords, PINs, OTPs, or card numbers.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may insist, reassure, or claim a "system requirement". They must not switch to asking for payments, app installs, or a different credential mechanism (that is jr_13). The legitimate caller must not ask for any credential or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: joiner details, bonus amount, and "credit" framing identical across cases
_F net-banking user ID and password request at turn 7
_L account number, IFSC, name via portal with explicit no-credentials statement
may_vary: whether cheque or passbook is mentioned
must_not_emit: real bank names or net-banking portals
what the caller would do with the login

ambiguities: Bank account", "IFSC", "credit", and "today" appear in both cases; none is evidence. Account number and IFSC are safe to share for receiving money.
Knowing the bonus amount is not evidence of legitimacy (C03).

Near jr_13 (OTP disclosure during onboarding). Both are credential requests; the credential and pretext differ. Flagged for deduplication review; if one must go, keep jr_18 for the strong account-number-vs-password contrast.

evidence_references.claim: Genuine entities never ask for username/password, card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
Impostors share a few real personal details to gain confidence (C03)
Impostors cite urgency to obtain credentials (C02)
